html: Alveolar macrophages clear inhaled particles through scavenger receptors: MARCO and SR-A1 bind silica, titanium dioxide and carbon particles, CD36 and LOX-1 oxidised lipids, and the particles are taken up into phagolysosomes. Crystalline and fibrous particles that cannot be digested break the lysosomal membrane. Leaked cathepsins, potassium efflux and reactive oxygen species then activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, which turns on caspase-1, and caspase-1 releases the active cytokine IL-1β.
